title: Why is a negative times a negative positive?
examples: Why is minus times minus a plus?

explain.say: Let us find the answer with a pattern, not a rule to memorise. 3 lots of minus 2 is minus 6. See the 3 hops of 2 to the left? It is like owing 2 dollars to 3 friends.

draw.text: Why is a negative times a negative positive?

explain.say: Now 2 lots of minus 2 is minus 4. Only 2 hops this time. And 1 lot of minus 2 is minus 2. What do you notice about the answers?
Look at the hops on the board: minus 6, minus 4, minus 2, 0. Each time, the answer goes up by 2. And 0 lots of minus 2 is 0. Can you guess the next stop?
The pattern goes up 2 every time. So after 0 comes plus 2. That means minus 1 times minus 2 is plus 2. See the last reason glowing? The pattern must carry on.

because.note: Three lots of minus 2 is minus 6

because.label: Up 2 each time
because.ask: What pattern do the answers make?

because.label: Keep the pattern
because.note: One more step up 2 lands on +2
because.ask: Why must the pattern carry on?

explain.say: Brilliant thinking! One more step: minus 2 times minus 2 is plus 4. Maths stays fair only if a negative times a negative is positive. Wow: the same rule makes minus divided by minus positive too. Can you predict minus 3 times minus 2?

faq.a: It is minus 6. Three lots of minus 2 added together is minus 2, minus 2 and minus 2, which makes minus 6.

faq.q: What pattern do the answers make?
faq.a: In 3 times minus 2, then 2 times, then 1 times, then 0 times, the answers go minus 6, minus 4, minus 2, 0. They go up by 2 each step.
asks: Why do the answers go up by 2?

faq.q: Why must the pattern carry on?
faq.a: Multiplying follows the same rules for every number. If the pattern broke at zero, other rules of maths would break too. So minus 1 times minus 2 has to be plus 2.

faq.q: Is a negative divided by a negative positive?
faq.a: Yes. Dividing undoes multiplying, so the sign rules match. Minus 8 divided by minus 2 is plus 4.

faq.q: What is a negative times a positive?
faq.a: It is negative. 3 times minus 2 is minus 6, and minus 3 times 2 is also minus 6.

facts: A negative times a negative is always positive: −3 × −4 = 12.
Brahmagupta wrote in 628 CE that the product of two debts is a fortune.

quiz.why: A negative times a negative is positive, and 4 times 5 is 20.

wrong.1: Minus 20 is the answer for a negative times a positive.
wrong.2: Minus 9 adds the numbers instead of multiplying.

quiz.why: One negative and one positive give a negative, so it is minus 18.

wrong.1: 18 needs both numbers to have the same sign.
